land.text: Kartli around Tbilisi, ruled by Bagrat VI as King of Kartli-Imereti 1466-1478 until Constantine II 'challenged him'; Cliopatria draws it as its 'Kingdom of Georgia' row (27,616 km2 in 1468-1506)

predecessors.note: Infobox: predecessor Kingdom of Georgia, established 1478. Cliopatria's own 'Kingdom of Kartli' row begins in 1463 with a 130,082 km2 shape that is the whole of the unified kingdom, not Kartli.

land.text: the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti, into which Kartli merged in 1762 ('Union of Kartli and Kakheti: 1762'); Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' row, 54,778-55,276 km2 for 1763-1802

successors.note: Russia annexed the united kingdom in 1800 (page), finalized by the Treaty of Gulistan (1813). The row Cliopatria labels 'Kingdom of Georgia' for 1706-1762 is Kartli alone. [Reviewer eu-19-e, 2026-10-31: successor slug changed from kingdom-of-georgia to kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti: the infobox reads 'Succeeded by: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti', and kingdom-of-georgia ends in 1478 while kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti (eu-19-d) starts in 1762 with found counterpart kingdom-of-kartli.]

capitals.name: Tbilisi (Tiflis)
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Tbilisi, no years given. Held by the Ottomans from August 1578 to the Safavid recapture of 1603-1604 and again from 12 June 1723 to 1736.

correction.text: the eastern core (Kartli) as Cliopatria draws it from 1468; the 1463-1467 whole-kingdom shape should not be used for Kartli

keyframe_review.note: 130,082 km2 for 1463-1467 is the whole unified kingdom (Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' drew 127,772 km2 in 1422-1462), and it overlaps the shapes Cliopatria starts for Imereti, Mingrelia, Guria, Abkhazia and Kakheti in 1468. The page: 'Major disintegration of the Georgian kingdom dates from 1463 with the defeat of George VIII at the Battle of Chikhori'; Bagrat VI 'proclaimed himself King of all Georgia in 1466'; George VIII ruled the Kakheti rump; Kartli's own kingdom is 'Established: 1478'. These years belong to the kingdom-of-georgia dossier; the shape for Kartli itself is Cliopatria's eastern 'Kingdom of Georgia' shape of 1468.

correction.text: Kartli as Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' shape of 1478, carried to 1578

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1478-1578: the page's Kartli kingdom begins in 1478 ('Constantine II ruled from 1478 to 1505') and Cliopatria gives the land to its 'Kingdom of Georgia' row (27,616-27,810 km2). The page gives no area and no extent beyond Tbilisi, so the shape is a re-attribution, not a verification. The 1513-1519 conquest of Kakheti and Constantine's 1481-1483 hold on Samtskhe are events.

correction.text: Kartli as an Ottoman tributary kingdom, 1579-1611, with Tbilisi garrisoned by the Ottomans from August 1578 to 1604

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1579-1611, a Cliopatria gap (its Ottoman row probably covers it). Page: 'From 1578 and for more than 40 years this Georgian Kingdom was under suzerainty of Ottoman Empire', paying tribute 'in boys, girls, horses, and wine'. The 1612 shape is used because it is the only Kartli-sized outline Cliopatria gives for the period; it is half the size of the 1478-1578 shape and the page cannot say which is right.

14,860 km2 for 1612-1701, a Kartli outline about half the size of the 27,616 km2 shape Cliopatria draws for 1468-1578 and the 31,452 km2 it draws for 1706-1762; the page gives no area, so the discrepancy is flagged, not resolved. '1612: the sultan accepted reinstatement of the 1555 Amasya Treaty excluding the Ottomans from Kartli and Kakhetia'; Kartli returned to Persian vassalage (infobox: Persia 1612-1723).
14,860 km2 for 1702-1705, the identical outline. The page gives no event for 1702; Cliopatria's change of shape id is a bookkeeping break. Unverified: page silent.

correction.text: Kartli as Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' shape of 1706, carried to 1762, including 1738-1743

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1706-1762: after 1705 Cliopatria draws Kartli under its 'Kingdom of Georgia' row (31,452-31,548 km2) and has no shape for 1738-1743. The page keeps the kingdom throughout ('with several brief intervals, until 1762') under Ottoman vassalage 1723-1736 and Persian 1736-1747; Teimuraz II ruled it from 1744 (footnote). The 1706 Cliopatria outline is used.

region.text: Kartli, the eastern core of the dissolved Georgian kingdom, capital Tbilisi

ledger.note: 1478: Constantine II founds the Kingdom of Kartli at Tbilisi. Infobox 'Established: 1478'; 'Bagrat VI ruled Kartli until 1478, when Constantine challenged him. Constantine II ruled from 1478 to 1505.' Constantine had been a 'de facto ruler in part of Kartli in 1469'.

region.text: Samtskhe, subordinated by Constantine II in 1481

ledger.note: 1481: Constantine II subordinates Samtskhe. 'In 1481 he subordinated Samtskhe and proclaimed himself King of All Georgia.'

region.text: Samtskhe, free of Kartli after the defeat at Ardeti

ledger.note: 1483: Samtskhe throws off Kartli. 'In 1483, Qvarqvare II defeated Constantine's forces at Ardeti.' The page does not say the subordination ended then; that is a reading.

region.text: Kakheti, conquered by Kartli under David X

ledger.note: 1513: Kartli briefly conquers Kakheti. 'In 1513, Kartli briefly conquered Kakheti, and in 1520 Levan restored Kakheti.'

1520: Levan restores Kakheti. 'In 1520 Levan restored Kakheti.' The Kakheti page puts Levan's kingship after Ismail I's invasion (the Kartli page dates Ismail's capture of Tbilisi to 1522 or 1524) and says 'a two-year war followed, and Kartli recognized Kakhetian independence'.

August 1578: the Ottomans take Tiflis. Lala Mustafa Pasha's campaign took 'Tiflis in August 1578' while 'pressing Kartli to become an Ottoman tributary'; Kartli page: 'From 1578 and for more than 40 years this Georgian Kingdom was under suzerainty of Ottoman Empire.' The Ottoman is the occupier (owner's record, roles reversed). The war page does not describe a garrison; the occupation of the city is a reading, and the kingdom beyond it is an Ottoman tributary.

1603-1604: Abbas I retakes Tbilisi. 'Safavid armies captured Tbilisi and both Kartli and Kakheti became Safavid dependencies once again' (the page's 1603-1604 section; no month). The Ottomans formally left Kartli only at the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha of 20 November 1612.
1632: Persia sets Rostom Khan over Kartli. 'In 1632, Rostom Khan was appointed as king/wali of Kartli'; he died in 1658. A change of ruling line inside a Persian-vassal state, which continues.

region.text: Kartli with Tbilisi, under Ottoman vassalage 1723-1736

ledger.note: 12 June 1723: an Ottoman army takes Tbilisi. 'In spring 1723 Konstantine used Iranian soldiers to capture Tbilisi. ... On 12 June an Ottoman army bloodlessly took Tbilisi from Konstantine.' Infobox: Ottoman vassal 1723-1736. The Ottoman is the occupier (owner's record, roles reversed).

region.text: Kartli with Tbilisi, released by the Ottomans in 1736

ledger.note: 1736: the Ottomans give up Kartli and Kakheti. 'In 1736, Turkey, at war with both Austria and Russia, gave up Kartli and Kakheti.' Infobox: Persian vassal 1736-1747.

region.text: Kartli, merged with Kakheti into the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti

ledger.note: 1762: Erekle II unites Kartli and Kakheti. 'In 1762, after Teimuraz II's death, Irakli II took control of Kartli and unified it with Kakheti' (infobox 'Union of Kartli and Kakheti: 1762'); the Kakheti page gives Teimuraz's death as 8 January.

region.text: the whole kingdom, merged into Kartli-Kakheti

ledger.note: 1762: the Kingdom of Kartli ends in the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti. The page: the kingdom existed 'with several brief intervals, until 1762,' when it merged with Kakheti; Russia annexed the united kingdom in 1800. [Reviewer eu-19-e, 2026-10-31: counterpart changed from kingdom-of-georgia to kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti, the dossier of the united kingdom.]

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1578-1590)
wars.outcome: Lala Mustafa Pasha took Tiflis in August 1578 and pressed Kartli to become a tributary; by the treaty of 21 March 1590 the Safavids ceded 'parts of Georgia' among much else.
wars.note: Kartli is the prize, not a belligerent with its own front; the contest between the two empires over Kartli (1578-1612) belongs to the ottoman-empire and safavid-dynasty dossiers, so the zones here are empty.

wars.name: Ottoman-Safavid War (1603-1618)
wars.outcome: Safavid armies captured Tbilisi in 1603-1604 and 'both Kartli and Kakheti became Safavid dependencies once again'; the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha (20 November 1612) 'secured the 1555 borders envisaged by the Peace of Amasya', i.e. Kartli to the Safavids.
wars.note: The war page gives no Georgian terms of its own; the Kartli page says the sultan accepted the 1555 treaty 'excluding the Ottomans from Kartli and Kakhetia' in 1612.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages; the frontiers of Kartli with Samtskhe, Imereti, Kakheti and the Persian and Ottoman lands are approximate. The Amasya line of 1555 and the Nasuh Pasha line of 1612 are treaty lines in principle but the pages describe them only as dividing 'eastern and western Georgia'.

sources.title: Kingdom of Kakheti
sources.note: Teimuraz II's death on 8 January 1762 and Levan's kingship; cross-check for 1513-1520.

sources.title: Peace of Amasya
sources.note: 29 May 1555: eastern Georgia in Iranian hands, western in Ottoman; no mention of Kartli by name.

sources.title: Ottoman-Safavid War (1578-1590)
sources.note: Tiflis taken in August 1578; 21 March 1590 treaty.

sources.title: Ottoman-Safavid War (1603-1618)

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages; five opened (the Kartli article is the source for almost every event; the Kakheti, Amasya and two war pages add cross-checks and the Tbilisi dates). Cliopatria problems for the reviewer: (1) the row 'Kingdom of Kartli' begins in 1463 with a 130,082 km2 shape that is the whole unified Georgia; the page dates Kartli's kingdom to 1478, so this dossier starts in 1478 and marks the 1463 shape wrong (years belong to kingdom-of-georgia). (2) Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' row (1468-1578 at 27.6k km2, 1706-1762 at 31.4k km2) is Kartli and not the whole kingdom: it borders Imereti and Kakheti, and in 1763 it grows by 23.8k km2, close to Kakheti's 23.4k. The kingdom-of-georgia dossier (another part of eu-19) should re-attribute 1468-1477 and 1579-1705 correctly; this dossier points its new keyframes at that row so the geometry is not duplicated. (3) The Kartli outline of 1612-1705 (14,860 km2) is half the size of the same state's shapes before and after; no page gives an area. Vassalage for the suzerain dossiers (from the Kartli infobox): Persia 1555-1578, Ottoman Empire 1578-1612, Persia 1612-1723, Ottoman Empire 1723-1736, Persia 1736-1747; Peace of Amasya (29 May 1555) 'recognized Kartli, Kakheti, and eastern Samtskhe as Persian possessions'. Shah Ismail's troops brought Tbilisi under control in 1522 or 1524 after David X's revolt (no end given): not ledgered. 1747: Teimuraz II and Heraclius II declared de facto independence. Teimuraz II is recorded as king of Kakheti 1732-1744 and of Kartli 1744-1762; the page gives no reign dates for Vakhtang VI beyond a footnote '(r. 1716-24)'. The page says Russia annexed the kingdom in 1800, not 1801. No rulers strip: the page gives only the first and last kings.
